chunks: 5091 - And al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

“If a wine drinker falls ill, do not visit him; if he dies, do not attend him; if he gives testimony, do not validate him; and if he proposes to you, do not marry him off. For whoever marries his daughter to a wine drinker, it is as though he has led her to zina. And whoever marries his daughter to one who opposes him in his religion has severed her kinship. And whoever entrusts a wine drinker, there shall be no guarantee for him with Allah, the Blessed and Exalted.”

key_terms.تَشْهَدُوهُ: attend him, here in the context of death/funeral presence
key_terms.تُزَكُّوهُ: declare him upright or validate his testimony
key_terms.تُزَوِّجُوهُ: marry him off or give a woman in marriage to him
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا: her kinship bond or family ties
key_terms.شَارِبُ الْخَمْرِ: a person who drinks wine; the central subject of the ruling

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about dealing with a wine drinker in marriage, testimony, and trust?
ai.summary: This hadith strongly condemns drinking wine and instructs the believers to withhold social and familial endorsement from a habitual wine drinker. It also warns against marrying one's daughter to such a person or to someone opposed in religion, and against placing trust in him, emphasizing the moral, legal, and social consequences of such conduct.
